A lecturer's pen tick marks this question as expected, and the lecturer has also corrected the printed answer in pen, inserting 'by' so the run-on sentence reads 'is achieved by ionospheric reflection'. Physics hand-checked: sky-wave propagation is long-distance communication by reflection of radio waves from the ionosphere, used by short-wave broadcast services in the band up to about 30 MHz; above about 30 MHz the wave passes through the ionosphere instead of being reflected.

recall_prompt: Say what sky wave propagation is — what reflects the wave — and which services use it, up to what frequency.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Reflection from the ionosphere
lines: Sky wave propagation is long-distance radio
communication in which the radio wave is
reflected by the ionosphere back to the
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word ionosphere and the word reflected must both appear.
steps.why: The reflection is what makes long distance possible: a wave sent up at a slant comes back down far away, well past the horizon that limits a straight-line wave. The book's printed sentence is a run-on; the lecturer's pen inserts 'by' to fix it — 'is achieved by ionospheric reflection'.
common_mistakes: Writing that the wave is reflected by the ground or by clouds. It is the ionosphere — the layer of charged particles in the upper atmosphere — that reflects it.
Confusing sky wave with space wave. A space wave travels in a straight line and is NOT reflected by the ionosphere.

recall.must_convey: That in sky wave propagation the radio wave is reflected by the ionosphere back to the earth, giving long-distance communication.
accept: the ionosphere reflects the wave back to earth
the wave goes up and the ionosphere sends it back down
reject: used for short-wave broadcast up to 30 megahertz

steps.memory_tip: Sky wave — the wave goes to the sky and the ionosphere returns it to the earth.

steps.label: Where it is used
steps.mark_note: Short-wave broadcast, up to about 30 MHz
lines: It is used by short-wave broadcast services
for frequencies up to about 30 MHz.
Above about 30 MHz the wave passes through
the ionosphere instead of being reflected.

lines.text: Sky wave: reflected by the ionosphere

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Short-wave services and the 30 MHz limit.
steps.why: The 30 MHz limit is physical, not a rule of thumb only: the ionosphere can turn back waves up to about this frequency, and higher-frequency waves go straight through — which is why TV and mobile signals need a different method.
common_mistakes: Writing 30 MHz as a lower limit. It is the UPPER limit — sky wave works up to about 30 MHz.
Saying television uses sky wave. TV frequencies are above 30 MHz and pass through the ionosphere, so TV uses space-wave methods instead.

recall.must_convey: That sky wave is used by short-wave broadcast services for frequencies up to about 30 MHz.
accept: above 30 megahertz the wave goes through the ionosphere

steps.memory_tip: Sky wave and short wave go together, and both stop at about 30 MHz.

insider_note: First mark: ionosphere + reflected, in one sentence. Second mark: short-wave broadcast and the 30 MHz upper limit. The lecturer's pen fixed the book's grammar here, not its physics.
